answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards. A harbor of independent validators checks that the stake is bonded and slashes it when an agent is caught coordinating fake accounts to evade limits. Reputation then follows the bonded identity across each thread of work, so splitting activity among sybils does not reset scrutiny. To attack at scale, an adversary must forge many costly deposits and risk losing them, rather than create free accounts.
